A '''Shop''' is any establishment which allows the trading of [[currencies|currency]] for an item or service, or vice versa. Shop prices may be lower or higher than the equivalent item's price on the [[Grand Exchange]], however, due to their fixed prices, shops cannot be susceptible to the market trends of the Grand Exchange.

==Stock==
Each shop has a maximum quantity of items in stock, which differs per item and per shop. Items can only be purchased in batches of 1, 5, 10 and 50. Whenever a shop has less of a certain item than their maximum capacity of that item, the shop will start to restock on that item. The time to restock varies between items. Only a single item will be re-added to the shop per restock, except in the case of [[Ore seller.]] which restocks items in batches. Items that aren't part of the shop's regular stock, or exceed their maximum capacity, will slowly be removed from the shop. Some shops, such as [[Grum's Gold Exchange.]] only have items with 0 stock, and so can only be sold to unless already overstocked from another player selling to them. Ironmen will not be able to purchase anything from these stores as any stocked items will be from other players. As they can only exist at 0 stock or overstocked, their "Restock" timer will only function as a "Destock" timer, and decrement the stock of any items back towards zero. There also exist shops such as [[The Flaming Arrow]] or [[Farming Supplies]] that have infinite stock, and are limited to only allowing the purchase of up to 10 items at a time.

Many shops have separate stock between [[Main account]]s and [[Ironmen]], and stock can be further separated between group, ultimate, and regular ironmen. For example, if an ultimate ironman buys ores from Ore seller, the shop's stock will not decrease for main accounts, group ironmen, or regular ironmen. However, if an ironman sells an item to the [[Pollnivneach general store]], all other account types will see the shop's stock increase.

Any shop that sells a [[Cape of Accomplishment]] has separate stock for players with and without level 99 in the respective skill, and further separate stock for players with that skill as their ''first'' 99, who can purchase an untrimmed cape.

Stock at any given shop always varies between [[worlds]], which some players use to their advantage by [[World switching|hopping worlds]] in order to trade items at the best prices through many small transactions. Multiple shops sometimes share the same stock; for example, buying an item at the [[Void Knight General Store]] decreases that item's stock at [[Jennifer's General Supplies]] in [[Shayzien]].

===Pricing===
Players may sell any tradeable item to a [[general store]] for a fixed [[value]] (usually its low alchemy value), or to specialty shops that specifically stock the item for a fixed higher value (usually its high alchemy value). These values will diminish by a fixed percentage that varies between shops for each stock increase. Regardless of how overstocked they are, all shops will buy the player's items for a minimum of 10% of the item's value. Players may buy any item in stock from a shop for a fixed value. This value will increase by the same fixed percentage mentioned previously for each stock decrease. Specialty shops use their maximum stock quantities as their fixed reference.

For example, a [[steel axe]] has a value of 200 [[coins]]. It can be sold to most general stores for 80 coins (40% of its value), should the shop not have any steel axes in stock. If the player were to sell it to an axe shop such as [[Bob's Brilliant Axes]], then it would sell for 120 coins (60% of its value), should [[Bob]] have his default quantity of 3 steel axes in stock. Since Bob has a fixed percentage change of 2% per sale, then selling a steel axe to him with 4 already in stock would yield 116 coins (58% of its value). If a player were to buy a steel axe from Bob with 3 in stock, it would cost 200 coins. If 4 steel axes were in stock, the price would be 196 coins (98% of its value).

==Features==
===Party chest===
Players can donate items to the [[Chest (Party Room)|Party Chest]], but cannot withdraw them again. 216 individual items can be put in, before the chest is full. Pulling the [[lever (Falador Party Room)|lever]] next to the chest for 1,000 [[coins]] will cause [[Party Balloon|balloons]] to float down around the Hall. Popping these balloons may yield an item from the chest. This, and the bar upstairs, makes the Party Hall a popular place for drop parties.

===Party Pete===
The owner of the Party Room, [[Party Pete]], is a fun-loving character. He will dance, chat, and give you a book titled [[Game book|Party Pete's Bumper Book of Games]]. He will also remove 'cheap' items from the Party Chest.

===Dancing knights===
Pulling the lever near the Party Chest will give a player the option of summoning the [[Knight (Falador Party Room)|dancing knights]] for 500 [[coins]]. The knights will dance on the tabletop, singing a song in homage to a similar scene in ''{{Wp|Monty Python and the Holy Grail}}''. The reference to the movie is further expanded upon in a dialogue with [[Party Pete]], who says that the knights of Camelot got it into their heads that the Party Room knights were making fun of them.

===Party announcement===
The [[Non-player character|NPCs]] in [[Falador]], such as the [[bank]] staff and the [[guard]]s, react with excitement when a party is about to take place, and will goad people towards the party room with even greater urgency when it is in progress. In order for the NPCs to start shouting {{overhead|Something is happening in the party room!}}, players must add items worth at least 50,000 [[coins]] in [[Grand Exchange]] value to the party chest, or items worth at least 76,000 coins in a [[members]]' worlds. After the lever is pulled, they will shout variations of {{overhead|Quick! Get to the party room!}} instead.

While one of the phrases said when a party is thrown refers to "big value items", this does not necessarily mean that the value of the party chest is concentrated in a few high-ticket items; any combination of items that together exceed the amounts stated above can trigger this announcement.

The party announcements only appear as overhead dialogue above the NPC's, not in the chatbox.

==Trivia==
*The party room was built in response to the large popularity of "drop parties". Many players were complaining about how people would cheat by just [[Telekinetic Grab|telegrabbing]] the item and making it impossible for other players to get anything. When built, it was just an empty building in which Telekinetic Grab was disabled. When the game was updated to RS2, the building became quite a bit more structured, adding the chest, lever, and bar. The Telegrab spell will still not work inside the party room, however.
*The party room was originally located in [[Seers' Village]]; it was, however, moved to [[Falador]] during the [[King's Ransom]] [[Quests|quest]] update to make room for the [[Seers' Village Courthouse|Courthouse]].

'''The Green Ghost''' is an inn found in [[Port Phasmatys]], a large seaport found in north-eastern [[Morytania]].

==History==
During Port Phasmatys' height, the Green Ghost was a very successful inn. The many [[pirate]]s from the [[Eastern Ocean|South-eastern ocean]] and the traders from the [[Eastern Lands]] brought with them business, adding to the town's already thriving populace. Since the town fell under the leadership of [[Necrovarus]], the inn has fallen into disrepair and is now run by ghosts. It has long since stopped selling [[beer]], as its pipes have run dry and supplies have become scarce.

==Brewery==
The inn's most popular attraction is its basement, where a small [[brewery]] is still maintained. Here players can brew a variety of ales and [[cider]]. Players can also purchase [[ale yeast]] from [[Metarialus]], provided they have a [[pot]] and 5 [[ectotoken]]s. This brewery is closer to a [[bank]] than the one in [[Keldagrim]], although the need for ectotokens makes it somewhat less accessible.

|40-100
|Skips the player's current assignment without penalties '''and''' permanently removes the assignment from the player's list of possible assignments - the player will not be assigned that monster again, unless they cancel the block. The cost varies between each Slayer master, with each master also having their own block list. 

Players can block the task as they obtain it, or they can block it straight from the "View List" option in the interface. Blocks will only be given for tasks that the player can access (indicated with a check mark); tasks that are not assigned, either due to not being toggled or players without the requirements cannot be blocked. This can also help players determine which tasks to block as each task has their own specific percentage of being assigned.

Blocking a task that is currently in [[Task Storage]] does not also skip it. If you wish to block and skip an undesired task, you should unstore it first.

There is a maximum limit of 7 types of assignments that can be blocked on one account - one block slot is given for every 50 quest points the player has. Currently there are six slots for a total of 300 points needed to use all of them. Additionally, one block slot is available once the player has completed the Elite tier of the [[Lumbridge & Draynor Diary]], which requires a [[quest cape]].
:'''Note:''' Cancelling the removal of monsters allows the monster to be assigned again, but '''does not''' refund points spent removing the monster.

<math>\begin{align}
Exp &= \left\lfloor\frac{Level^2}{600}\right\rfloor \times N

*The factor <math>N</math>:

*The <math>\lfloor\quad\rfloor</math> indicate that the expression should be rounded down to the nearest whole number.

===Upgrades===
A player can imbue certain items with Zeal Tokens. Imbuing an item provides bonuses and appends an [[(i)]] suffix to the item's name. Imbued items can be un-imbued, which removes the bonuses from the item and refunds 100% of the reward points used to imbue it.

Although the items available to imbue are the same as those from the [[Nightmare Zone]], items imbued at the Nightmare Zone cannot be unimbued for Zeal Tokens, nor vice versa. The cost of imbuing items is halved if you have claimed the hard-tier [[Combat Achievements]] rewards.

A '''stall''' is a stand that [[NPCs]] use to display their product. The majority of stalls can be stolen from with appropriate level in [[Thieving]]. Items sold include: [[silk]], [[fur]], [[scimitar]]s, [[fish]], [[vegetable]]s, etc. Most types of stalls can be found in [[Ardougne]]; however, there is also a selection in [[Rellekka]], [[Miscellania]], [[Sophanem]], [[Keldagrim]], [[Draynor]], [[Varrock]], [[Great Kourend]] and [[Prifddinas]]. Stealing from a stall may alert a nearby [[guard]] who will attack until they die, you unsuccessfully pickpocket them, or the area is left. To prevent guards/merchants from noticing you, thieve with the stall between your character and the NPC. Stall owners will not talk to players if they have stolen from their stall within the last 20 minutes (in-game time). It's not needed for the stalls found on [[Ape Atoll]].

'''Yrsa's Shoe Store''' was a shop in [[Rellekka]]. As well as [[Yrsa's Accoutrements|selling clothes]], [[Yrsa]] could change your shoe colour and style free of charge. Both access to the store's stock and the ability to change one's shoes required the completion of [[The Fremennik Trials]] [[quest]]. Visiting the store was a part of the [[easy Fremennik Diary]].

The shop has since been superseded by the [[makeover]] interface, also offered by Yrsa.
